questions.q: Why does the course use Vite rather than Create React App?
options: CRA is deprecated and no longer recommended; Vite is fast, nearly config-free and small enough to read
questions.explain: For routing and server rendering the React docs point to frameworks (Level 4).

questions.q: What does the -- in `npm create vite@latest react-lab -- --template react` do?
options: Passes --template react through npm to the Vite scaffolder
questions.explain: Use --template react-ts for TypeScript.

questions.q: What does src/main.jsx do?
questions.explain: App.jsx is the root component; vite.config.js enables the React plugin.

questions.q: What does the React plugin in vite.config.js provide?
options: The JSX transform and Fast Refresh
questions.explain: index.html is the entry point that Vite serves.

questions.q: What does JSX compile to?
options: Function calls that produce plain objects
questions.explain: That's why most JSX 'rules' are obvious consequences.

questions.q: What can go inside {} in JSX?
options: Expressions such as a ternary, &&, or .map(), not statements like if or for
questions.explain: Compute values above the return or use expression forms.

questions.q: Which are the correct JSX attribute names?
questions.explain: aria-* and data-* keep their dashes.

questions.q: Why use a fragment (<>…</>) instead of a div in a table row?
options: A component returns one value, and a div inside <tr> would be invalid HTML; fragments add nothing to the DOM
questions.explain: Use <Fragment key={id}> when a key is needed.

questions.q: What are props?
options: A component's arguments, collected into one object passed as the first argument
questions.explain: The usual style destructures them in the signature.

questions.q: When does the default `inStock = true` apply?
options: When the prop is missing or undefined, but not for null or false
questions.explain: It is an ordinary JavaScript default parameter.

questions.q: What is the children prop?
options: A list of child components in state
Whatever you put between a component's opening and closing tags
questions.explain: It is the basis of composition.

questions.q: How do children talk back to parents?
options: Through function props, such as onSelect
questions.explain: Parents decide what data a child gets; the child turns it into UI.

questions.q: After one click, what does n show for three `setN(n + 1)` calls starting from 0?
options: 1, because n is a constant snapshot of 0 in this render
questions.explain: All three calls say 'set it to 0 + 1'.

questions.q: How do you make three increments in one click add up to 3?
options: Call setN three times with n
questions.explain: React queues them and feeds each the previous result.

questions.q: Why does a plain `let count = 0` fail as a counter?
options: Changing it doesn't trigger a re-render, and it resets to 0 on every render
questions.explain: State lives outside the function call, managed by React.

questions.q: Why mutate-then-set (profile.city = 'Chennai'; setProfile(profile)) is a bug?
options: React compares with Object.is and sees the same object, so it may skip the update
questions.explain: Create a new object: setProfile({ ...profile, city: 'Chennai' }).

questions.q: What is the difference between onClick={handleSave} and onClick={handleSave()}?
options: The first passes a reference; the second runs handleSave during render and passes its return value
questions.explain: To pass arguments, wrap in an arrow function.

questions.q: How do you prevent a form's default submission in React?
options: Call e.preventDefault(); returning false doesn't work
questions.explain: The handler then reads data with FormData.

questions.q: When does onChange fire on a text input in React?
options: On every keystroke, like the DOM input event
questions.explain: It doesn't wait for the field to lose focus.

questions.q: What does e.stopPropagation() in a delete button inside a clickable card do?
options: Stops the click from also reaching the card's onOpen
questions.explain: Events bubble up the component tree.

questions.q: What renders for {messages.length && <MessageList />} when messages is empty?
questions.explain: React renders numbers; use messages.length > 0 &&.

questions.q: Which branching style suits cases where whole outputs differ?
questions.explain: Ternaries suit two small inline pieces; && suits 'show this or nothing'.

questions.q: What happens to a component's state when it returns null?
options: The component still exists and keeps its state; it just produces no DOM
questions.explain: Example: a Toast with no message.

questions.q: How do you turn an array into elements?
options: With .map(), giving each element a stable key
questions.explain: Keys help React match items between renders.

questions.q: What is a controlled input?
options: React owns the value through state, and every keystroke updates state
questions.explain: React is then the single source of truth.

questions.q: What happens if you give an input value without onChange?
options: It becomes read-only and React warns; use defaultValue for an uncontrolled starting value
questions.explain: defaultValue sets the initial value of an uncontrolled input.

questions.q: What does `setForm(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: value }))` allow?
options: One handler serves every field, using a computed property key from the input's name
questions.explain: The name attribute must match a key in the state object.

questions.q: How do you read a checkbox in a handler?
questions.explain: Text, select and textarea use e.target.value, a string.

questions.q: When does an effect with the dependency array [] run?
options: After mount only (and again on remount)
questions.explain: Omitting the array runs it after every render; [a, b] runs when they change.

questions.q: When does React call an effect's cleanup function?
options: Before re-running the effect with new dependencies, and on unmount
questions.explain: Without cleanup, every remount would leave another interval running.

questions.q: Why does StrictMode run effects twice in development?
options: It mounts, unmounts and remounts to test that cleanup is correct
questions.explain: With correct cleanup, the visible behaviour is identical.

questions.q: What is the right response to a react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warning?
options: Fix the cause; every reactive value the effect reads belongs in the array
questions.explain: The rule is enabled in the Vite template.

questions.q: What do CSS Modules (*.module.css) provide?
options: Generated unique class names, so one component's .button can't clash with another's, at zero runtime cost
questions.explain: You still write normal CSS.

questions.q: What are inline styles in React good and poor for?
options: Good for truly dynamic values; poor for :hover, media queries and pseudo-elements
questions.explain: Numbers get px for most length properties: { margin: 8 } → 8px.

questions.q: What is the hybrid for dynamic values?
options: Pass them through CSS custom properties, such as style={{ '--pct': ... }}
questions.explain: The CSS then uses var(--pct) and keeps :hover and transitions.

questions.q: What is the problem with plain global CSS in a big app?
options: Every .btn anywhere gets the rules, so collisions creep in
questions.explain: It's fine for resets, typography and tokens.

questions.q: Where does the list of expenses live in the tracker, and why?
options: In App, because the list, summary and form all need it
questions.explain: Form field values stay in ExpenseForm because nobody else cares until submit.

questions.q: Which data is derived rather than state?
options: The filtered list, totals and breakdown, computed in App during render
questions.explain: Ask: who needs it, and can it be computed from something else?

questions.q: What does monthKey("2026-09-14") return with isoDate.slice(0, 7)?
questions.explain: It's used for the month filter.

questions.q: What is the caveat with today() using toISOString()?
options: It's UTC, so near midnight it may be off by a day in some time zones
questions.explain: A production app would format the local date instead.

questions.q: What problem does composition solve compared with a 'god component'?
options: Instead of a prop for every variation, the parent passes pieces of UI
questions.explain: Every new design would otherwise add another prop and conditional.

questions.q: How do you give a layout several regions?
options: Pass JSX through ordinary props like header and sidebar, plus children
questions.explain: JSX elements are values that can be passed around.

questions.q: Why build ConfirmDelete out of a generic Dialog?
options: Dialog stays generic and never learns about 'delete'; the specific component is thin and readable
questions.explain: It's specialisation through composition.

questions.q: What is a render prop?
options: A prop that is a function returning UI
questions.explain: It lets the parent control a slot that depends on the child's data.

questions.q: In which direction does React data flow?
questions.explain: Two components can't 'reach across' to each other.

questions.q: What fixes two panels that need to coordinate as an accordion?
options: Lift the open state to their closest common parent and pass it and callbacks down
questions.explain: Remove state from the children, pass values down, add state to the parent.

questions.q: What does `setOpenId(current => (current === id ? null : id))` do?
options: Toggles: opens this panel, or closes it if already open, so only one is open
questions.explain: The parent stores only the id of the open panel.

questions.q: Why is lifting state described as the most important structural decision?
options: It decides which component owns each piece of data
questions.explain: Wrong ownership leads to duplication and sync bugs.

questions.q: What does a reducer take and return?
options: The current state and an action; it returns the next state
questions.explain: Handlers report what happened rather than how to change state.

questions.q: What must a reducer be?
options: Pure: no mutation, API calls, randomness or reading the current time
questions.explain: It is a plain function outside the component.

questions.q: How should actions be named?
questions.explain: It keeps the reducer a record of what the user did and lets one action update several fields consistently.

questions.q: When does useReducer beat useState?
options: Several values change together, updates are complex, or you want to unit test transitions without rendering
questions.explain: For one or two independent values useState is simpler.

questions.q: What is prop drilling?
options: Passing a prop through several components that don't use it so a deep one can
questions.explain: Context lets any descendant read the value directly.

questions.q: When is the default value passed to createContext used?
options: Only when there is no provider above the consumer
questions.explain: The three steps are create, provide, consume.

questions.q: Why wrap context in a provider component and a custom hook that throws without the provider?
options: It turns 'forgot the provider' into a clear error instead of a confusing undefined
questions.explain: The null default plus the throwing useAuth does this.

questions.q: Why does the AuthProvider wrap its value in useMemo?
options: So consumers don't re-render just because the provider re-rendered with a new object
questions.explain: The memo depends on [user]. Note the lesson says real authentication needs a server.

questions.q: What is a custom hook?
options: A function whose name starts with use and which calls other hooks
questions.explain: You share the logic, not the component.

questions.q: What does useOnlineStatus return?
options: A boolean online value, kept up to date by online/offline listeners with cleanup
questions.explain: Both components then use it instead of copying the effect.

questions.q: Does calling the same custom hook in two components share state between them?
options: No: each call gets its own state
questions.explain: Hooks share logic, not state.

questions.q: Which Rules of Hooks apply?
options: Call hooks only at the top level of components or custom hooks, not in loops, conditions or nested functions
questions.explain: React relies on the call order being the same on every render.

questions.q: Why does a single status field ('idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error') beat separate isLoading and isError booleans?
options: The booleans could contradict each other
questions.explain: One status models states explicitly.

questions.q: Why check res.ok after fetch?
options: fetch only rejects on network failure, so a 404 or 500 would otherwise be treated as success
questions.explain: The code throws Error(`Request failed: ${res.status}`).

questions.q: What does returning () => controller.abort() from the effect achieve?
options: It cancels the in-flight request when userId changes or the component unmounts, avoiding out-of-order responses
questions.explain: The catch ignores AbortError because we cancelled it ourselves.

questions.q: What were the problems of the naive useEffect fetch?
options: No loading indicator, swallowed errors, 404/500 treated as success, and nothing handles changing inputs
questions.explain: The lesson notes most production apps eventually hand this job to a library or framework.

questions.q: What does Outlet do in a layout route?
options: Renders the matching child route, while the header stays mounted
questions.explain: The layout wraps all child pages.

questions.q: What does path="products/:productId" define, and how is it read?
options: A dynamic segment, read with useParams()
questions.explain: For example /products/42.

questions.q: What does <Route path="*"> do?
options: Catches everything else, serving as the 404 page
questions.explain: index marks the child shown at the parent's exact path.

questions.q: What does NavLink's end prop do on to="/"?
questions.explain: NavLink adds an active class and aria-current="page" when its route matches.

questions.q: Which things cause a component to re-render?
options: Its own state change, its parent re-rendering, or a context it reads changing
questions.explain: Props change only because the parent re-rendered.

questions.q: Is a re-render the same as a DOM update?
options: No: React re-runs your function, diffs the result, and touches the DOM only where output differs
questions.explain: Most re-renders are cheap.

questions.q: What should you do before reaching for memo, useMemo or useCallback?
options: Measure with the Profiler on a production build and try structural fixes like moving state down
questions.explain: Dev mode is slower and double-renders in StrictMode.

questions.q: Why move the query state into a Search component rather than Dashboard?
options: So typing doesn't re-render the expensive chart
questions.explain: State lives where it's used.

questions.q: What roles do Vitest and React Testing Library play?
options: Vitest runs the tests (sharing Vite's config); RTL renders components and finds elements
questions.explain: jsdom simulates the DOM in Node; jest-dom adds matchers like toBeInTheDocument().

questions.q: Which query does RTL put first in priority?
questions.explain: getByTestId is the last resort.

questions.q: What do getBy, queryBy differ in when nothing matches?
options: getBy throws; queryBy returns null (for asserting something is absent)
questions.explain: Use getBy for elements that should be there now.

questions.q: In the Counter test with initial={2}, what is expected after one click on Increment?
questions.explain: user.click is awaited, then the text is asserted.

questions.q: Where does the search query live in the Recipe Finder?
questions.explain: URL state makes searches shareable and bookmarkable.

questions.q: What does the project's toRecipe normalisation do?
options: Converts the API's strIngredient1…20 fields into a clean ingredients array, keeping API shapes out of components
questions.explain: It's done once in api.js.

questions.q: What does TheMealDB return when nothing matches?
questions.explain: Handle null explicitly.

questions.q: How are favourites persisted and shared?
options: Through a context and reducer, persisted in localStorage, with a count in the header on every page
questions.explain: The project reuses the useFetch and debounced-value hooks too.

questions.q: Which are React's three phases?
questions.explain: Rendering means calling your functions, not painting pixels.

questions.q: What happens in the render phase?
options: React calls component functions and compares with the previous output; no DOM is touched, and it can be interrupted in concurrent rendering
questions.explain: The commit phase applies changes and is never interrupted.

questions.q: What happens when a span switches to an input at the same position?
options: The span and everything below it is destroyed and a new input is created
The span is updated in place
questions.explain: Different types produce different trees.

questions.q: Why does React use heuristics instead of a general tree diff?
options: The general algorithm is around O(n³), too slow; heuristics based on types and keys make it linear
questions.explain: The two assumptions: different types give different trees; keys identify stable children.

questions.q: What is the key distinction that removes most of the need for a store?
options: Server state (data living on a server) versus client state (UI state existing only in the browser)
questions.explain: Server state is best handled by a caching library; what's left for a store is usually small.

questions.q: How does a Zustand component avoid re-rendering on unrelated changes?
options: It passes a selector and re-renders only when the selected value changes
questions.explain: AddToCart selects a function that never changes, so cart updates don't re-render it.

questions.q: Why is `useCartStore(s => ({ items: s.items, clear: s.clear }))` a problem?
options: It builds a new object every time, so it re-renders on every store change
questions.explain: Select separately or use useShallow.

questions.q: Does Zustand need a provider?
options: No; the store is a module-level singleton
questions.explain: set merges returned partial state one level deep.

questions.q: How does TanStack Query treat server data?
options: As a cache that can go stale, not as state you own
questions.explain: It adds caching, deduplication, background refresh and mutation handling.

questions.q: What does queryKey ['todos'] mean for multiple components?
options: They share one cache entry and one request
questions.explain: The key must include every variable the query depends on, like a dependency array.

questions.q: What is the difference between isPending and isFetching?
options: isPending means no data yet; isFetching means a request is in flight, including background refetches
questions.explain: That lets you show 'Refreshing…' over old data.

questions.q: Why must queryFn throw on a non-OK response?
options: Otherwise failed responses would be treated as data; the query only sees errors through rejected promises
questions.explain: The lesson uses an res.ok check.

questions.q: Why is <button type="button" onClick={save}> better than <div onClick={save}>?
options: It's focusable, activated by Enter/Space, and announced as a button
questions.explain: The first rule of ARIA: don't use ARIA when a native element does the job.

questions.q: What does alt="" mean on an image?
options: It's decorative and skipped by screen readers
questions.explain: Informative images need meaningful alt text.

questions.q: Why use useId for label and input ids?
options: Hard-coded ids break when a component renders twice
questions.explain: It also builds aria-describedby ids.

questions.q: What does :focus-visible do?
options: Shows the focus ring for keyboard users without showing it on mouse click
questions.explain: Never remove outlines without replacing them.

questions.q: How does React Hook Form register inputs by default?
options: Uncontrolled, reading values from the DOM via refs, so typing doesn't re-render the whole form
questions.explain: That's why it scales to larger forms.

questions.q: What does z.coerce.number() do?
options: Converts the string from an input into a number before checking it
questions.explain: Inputs always give strings.

questions.q: What does .refine on a Zod object do in the lesson?
options: Adds a cross-field rule (end date on or after start) and attaches the error to endDate
questions.explain: The path option attaches the error to a field.

questions.q: What is the benefit of describing the data once in a schema?
options: It removes the need for forms
It validates everywhere, on client and ideally the server too
questions.explain: zodResolver connects the schema to React Hook Form.

questions.q: What happens to the app when an error is thrown during render with no error boundary?
options: The entire app unmounts, leaving a blank page
questions.explain: An error boundary limits the damage to its subtree.

questions.q: Which feature still requires a class component?
questions.explain: They use getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatch.

questions.q: Which errors does an error boundary NOT catch?
options: Errors in event handlers and in async code like setTimeout or promise callbacks
questions.explain: For event handlers use try/catch and set error state.

questions.q: What does <Suspense fallback> do?
options: Shows a fallback while something inside is still loading
questions.explain: Both Suspense and boundaries handle 'not ready' and 'went wrong' declaratively.

questions.q: What does a dynamic import('./reports') do under Vite?
options: Becomes a separate chunk (reports-[hash].js) fetched when the line runs
questions.explain: A static import goes in the main bundle.

questions.q: What does React.lazy require of the imported module?
options: A default export that is a component
questions.explain: For named exports map them to { default: m.Name }.

questions.q: Why call lazy at module level, not inside a component?
options: Otherwise each render creates a new lazy type and remounts
questions.explain: A lazy component also needs a <Suspense> above it.

questions.q: Why are routes natural places to split?
options: Users visit one page at a time
questions.explain: Every user would otherwise download the admin panel before the login page.

questions.q: What does React.ReactNode mean as a prop type?
options: Anything renderable: elements, strings, numbers, null, arrays of those
questions.explain: It's the usual type for children.

questions.q: How do you make a wrapper accept every native button attribute?
questions.explain: Then disabled, onClick and aria-* all type-check.

questions.q: What file extension holds JSX in a typed project?
questions.explain: Start with --template react-ts; types come from @types/react and @types/react-dom.

questions.q: What is the advantage of string-literal unions such as 'primary' | 'secondary' in props?
questions.explain: React.FC is no longer recommended as a default; plain functions are simpler.

questions.q: Which technique is called the cheapest and most robust for UI animation?
options: CSS transitions driven by a state-changed class
questions.explain: The element stays mounted; only a class changes.

questions.q: Which properties are cheap to animate?
options: transform and opacity, which run on the compositor without layout
questions.explain: Width, height, top and left force layout work every frame.

questions.q: Why are exit animations hard in React?
options: React removes the DOM node immediately, leaving nothing to animate, so you must keep it mounted until the exit finishes
questions.explain: The useDelayedUnmount hook keeps it mounted for ms before removing.

questions.q: What does the inert attribute on a hidden drawer do?
options: Removes its contents from the tab order and accessibility tree
questions.explain: React 19 supports it as a boolean attribute.

questions.q: Where does server data versus UI-only state live in the Kanban project?
options: Cards in TanStack Query; selected card and filters in a small Zustand store
questions.explain: This is the server-state versus client-state split.

questions.q: What happens in an optimistic move if the server fails?
questions.explain: Optimistic updates show the result immediately, with rollback on failure.

questions.q: How can cards be moved?
options: By mouse drag and drop and by keyboard buttons as an accessible alternative
questions.explain: Accessibility is a project requirement.

questions.q: What does json-server provide?
options: A local REST API on db.json with GET/POST /cards and GET/PATCH/DELETE /cards/:id
questions.explain: Its CLI flags have changed across versions.

questions.q: What is true of React Server Components?
options: They run only on the server or at build time; their code never ships to the browser, only their rendered output
questions.explain: RSC requires a framework or bundler integration, such as Next.js's App Router; you can't flip a switch in a plain Vite app.

questions.q: What can a Server Component do that a Client Component cannot?
options: Read databases, files and secrets directly, and be async
questions.explain: The table lists the opposite set for Client Components.

questions.q: How do you opt a module into the client in an RSC app?
options: The 'use client' directive at the top of the file
questions.explain: Components are Server Components by default.

questions.q: What does the database library in a Server Component add to the browser bundle?
questions.explain: The component awaits its data where the data lives, with no useEffect or loading state.

questions.q: What problem does concurrent rendering solve?
options: A slow render freezing the page, including the text box being typed in
questions.explain: React can prepare an update in the background, interrupt it, and discard it if outdated.

questions.q: In useTransition's handleChange, which update is urgent?
options: setQuery, so the input shows the character now
questions.explain: The filter update inside startTransition is non-urgent and may lag.

questions.q: What happens when the user types again before a transition render finishes?
options: React abandons the in-progress render and restarts with the latest value
questions.explain: isPending is true while the transition is in progress.

questions.q: What should you do with isPending?
options: Dim stale content rather than blanking it
questions.explain: The demo SlowRow adds artificial slowdown to show the effect.

questions.q: Which Core Web Vital shows React rendering performance most directly?
questions.explain: A click triggering a 300 ms render is a 300 ms+ interaction.

questions.q: What is the difference between lab and field data?
options: Lab data is measured on your machine (Lighthouse, dev tools); field data comes from real users, e.g. via the web-vitals library
questions.explain: Real users on mid-range phones are the ones who matter.

questions.q: Which Profiler view is usually the fastest way to find the culprit?
options: Ranked, which sorts components by own render time
questions.explain: Selecting a component shows why it rendered.

questions.q: What does 'Props changed: onSelect' on a memo component usually signal?
options: An unstable callback is defeating memoization
questions.explain: It's a classic signal.

questions.q: Why should components reference tokens rather than raw hex values?
options: Theming, such as dark mode or a second brand, becomes a matter of redefining tokens
questions.explain: Larger systems keep tokens in a neutral format like JSON and generate CSS, iOS and Android outputs from one source.

questions.q: What do headless libraries (Radix Primitives, React Aria, Headless UI) provide?
options: Behaviour and ARIA without styles, so you add your own look
questions.explain: The hard parts are focus trapping, keyboard navigation, typeahead and positioning.

questions.q: What is a design system?
options: A shared set of decisions (colours, spacing, type, interaction patterns) packaged as reusable components and documentation
questions.explain: Done badly it's a pile of over-configurable components everyone works around.

questions.q: How is dark theme applied in the tokens example?
questions.explain: Components don't change.

questions.q: What is the benefit of organising by feature rather than by file type?
options: Everything about invoices lives in one folder, and deleting a feature deletes one folder
questions.explain: Ownership also maps cleanly to teams with CODEOWNERS.

questions.q: What may a feature import from?
options: shared and other features' public APIs only
questions.explain: Each feature exposes its public API through index.ts.

questions.q: How can the dependency rules be enforced?
options: With lint rules such as no-restricted-imports blocking deep imports into another feature
questions.explain: Pattern: '@/features/*/*'.

questions.q: What should you do if invoices and customers need each other?
options: Extract the shared concept into shared or a new feature, or have app compose them
questions.explain: No cycles between features.

questions.q: Why does React render '' as literal text?
options: Strings are inserted as text nodes, so the browser never parses them as HTML
questions.explain: Attribute values are likewise set as values, not injected into markup.

questions.q: When is dangerouslySetInnerHTML an XSS hole?
options: When the HTML is influenced by users, even via your own API
questions.explain: Sanitize with a maintained library such as DOMPurify, or avoid HTML strings.

questions.q: Why not write your own sanitizer with regular expressions?
options: HTML parsing has many edge cases (malformed tags, encodings, SVG and MathML namespaces) that attackers exploit
questions.explain: Use a well-maintained sanitizer.

questions.q: What is the risk of <a href={user.website}>?
options: A javascript: URL runs script on click, because React escapes text but a URL is a value the browser acts on
questions.explain: Validate URL schemes. Authorisation, validation and secrets belong on the server.

questions.q: Where does the 'testing trophy' say most effort should go?
options: Integration tests, with a broad static base, solid unit tests and thin E2E
questions.explain: It's a heuristic, not a law.

questions.q: What do integration tests with MSW mock?
options: Only the network, so real fetch, TanStack Query setup and error handling all run
questions.explain: MSW intercepts at the network layer.

questions.q: What should E2E tests cover?
options: A handful of critical journeys like sign up, log in and checkout
questions.explain: They catch routing, build config, real browser APIs and the backend contract.

questions.q: What should you not test?
options: Implementation details, third-party libraries' own behaviour, trivial markup
questions.explain: Such tests break on refactors without catching real bugs.

questions.q: Why must you never put secrets in VITE_ variables?
options: They're replaced at build time, so the literal string ends up in the public JavaScript bundle
questions.explain: Changing a value also requires a rebuild; use runtime config if one build serves many environments.

questions.q: What is the SPA fallback for?
options: Serving index.html for unknown paths so reloading /invoices/42 works with BrowserRouter
questions.explain: Real files like /assets/*.js are still served normally.

questions.q: Why are hashed asset filenames served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable?
options: The filename changes when content changes, so they can be cached for a year
questions.explain: index.html should not be cached that long.

questions.q: Why test npm run preview before deploying?
options: Some bugs (env vars, base paths, case-sensitive imports on Linux) only appear in the build
questions.explain: It serves dist/ locally.

questions.q: Why can't you build translated sentences by concatenating fragments?
questions.explain: Use message catalogs with interpolation.

questions.q: What do Intl APIs provide without a library?
options: Locale-aware formatting of numbers, currency, dates, relative times, lists and plural rules
questions.explain: You never hand-format them.

questions.q: Why cache Intl formatter instances?
options: Constructing Intl objects is relatively expensive
questions.explain: The lesson caches by `${locale}|${currency}`.

questions.q: How many plural forms do languages have?
options: It varies: English has two, some languages one, Arabic has six categories
questions.explain: That's why plural rules come from Intl.PluralRules or the catalog library.

questions.q: What backend options does the capstone offer?
options: A local mock server (json-server or MSW), your own small API, or an RSC framework
questions.explain: Write down your choice and why in an ADR.

questions.q: Where should filter and sort state live for the task table?
questions.explain: It makes views shareable and bookmarkable.

questions.q: Which non-functional requirements does the capstone set?
options: Accessibility with zero axe violations on key screens, a JS budget enforced in CI, good INP, errors contained per widget, strict TypeScript
questions.explain: CI runs lint, types, tests, E2E and build.

questions.q: What is the capstone's learning approach?
options: A specification, decisions, milestones and a review checklist rather than a copy-along tutorial
questions.explain: Plan for a few weeks of part-time work.
pen is added twice (qty 2, 20) plus ink once (50) = 70.

questions.q: Continuing from the previous cart (pen qty 2, ink qty 1), what is the state after `{ type: 'qty_set', id: 1, qty: 0 }`?
options: Only ink remains, because items with qty 0 are filtered out
questions.explain: The reducer maps the change and then filters out quantities of 0 or less. Verified by running it.

questions.q:
Why does the reducer return new arrays and objects instead of mutating?
```javascript
const before = [{ id: 1, qty: 1 }]
const after = cartReducer(before, { type: 'added', item: { id: 1 } })
console.log(before === after, before[0].qty, after[0].qty)
```
options: The new state is a different array, and the old value is untouched: false 1 2
questions.explain: React compares state with Object.is, so a changed result must be a new reference; printed output is `false 1 2`.

questions.q: What does the reducer do with an unknown action type like { type: 'x' }?
questions.explain: The default branch throws, which surfaces typos in action names.

questions.q: A click handler runs `setN(n + 1)` three times with n = 0 in this render. What is n after the re-render?
options: 1, because n is the constant 0 in this render's snapshot
questions.explain: All three calls say 'set it to 0 + 1'.

questions.q: Using updater functions, `setN(p => p + 1)` three times in one click starting from 0 gives:
questions.explain: React queues the functions and feeds each the previous result. Simulating the queue gives 3.

questions.q: In one handler: `setN(5); setN(p => p * 2)` starting from 0. What is n afterwards?
questions.explain: 5 is queued as a value, then the updater doubles it. (A function followed by a value, like `setN(p => p + 1); setN(10)`, ends at 10: the last one wins.)

questions.q:
React decides whether state changed using Object.is. Which result is correct?
```javascript
console.log(Object.is(NaN, NaN), Object.is(0, -0), Object.is({}, {}))
```
questions.explain: NaN is the same as NaN, 0 and -0 differ, and two separate objects are different references. Verified by running it.

questions.q: With `{messages.length && <MessageList />}` and an empty messages array, what appears?
questions.explain: 0 is a number React renders. Use messages.length > 0 &&.

questions.q:
What does this print for tasks = [done a, not-done b, done c]?
```javascript
console.log(tasks.filter(t => t.done).map(t => t.id).join(','))
```
questions.explain: filter keeps done tasks and map takes their ids.

questions.q: When does `useEffect(fn, [])` run?
options: After mount only (and again if remounted, such as in StrictMode in development)
questions.explain: An omitted array runs after every render; [a, b] re-runs when they change.

questions.q: Which cleanup behaviour is correct for an effect that starts setInterval?
options: Return () => clearInterval(id); React runs it before re-running the effect and on unmount
Cleanup only runs on page reload
questions.explain: Without it, each remount leaves another interval running.

questions.q: Two components both call useOnlineStatus(). How much state is shared?
options: None: each call gets its own state; hooks share logic, not state
questions.explain: To share state, lift it up or use context or a store.

questions.q: Which is the correct place for state that two sibling components both need to read and change?
options: Each sibling, kept in sync with effects
Their closest common parent, passed down with callbacks
questions.explain: This is lifting state up.

questions.q: What does the TanStack Query key ['todos', id] do?
options: Uses one entry for all ids
Identifies a separate cache entry per id; switching back reuses the cached data
questions.explain: The key includes every variable the query depends on, like a dependency array.

questions.q: What happens to an error thrown in an event handler with an error boundary above it?
options: It is not caught by the boundary; use try/catch and set error state
questions.explain: Boundaries catch errors during rendering, lifecycle methods and constructors, not event handlers or async code.

questions.q: Why must lazy() be called at module level?
options: Otherwise each render creates a new lazy type and remounts the component
questions.explain: A lazy component also needs a <Suspense> boundary above it.

questions.q: What does startTransition mark as low priority?
options: The updates inside it, so urgent input updates stay responsive and an outdated render can be abandoned
questions.explain: isPending is true while the transition runs.

questions.q: Why can't you set secrets in VITE_ environment variables?
options: They are replaced at build time and end up in the public JavaScript bundle
questions.explain: Authorisation, validation and secrets belong on the server.

questions.q: What is the right use of dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user-provided rich text?
options: Sanitize with a maintained library like DOMPurify, or avoid HTML strings entirely
questions.explain: Regex sanitizers miss many HTML edge cases.

challenges.title: Cart reducer
challenges.prompt: Write cartReducer(state, action) for a shopping cart. Actions: { type: 'added', item } (increase qty if the id exists, else add with qty 1), { type: 'removed', id }, and { type: 'qty_set', id, qty } (items with qty <= 0 are removed). Unknown types must throw `Unknown action: <type>`. Never mutate state.
challenges.starter:
function cartReducer(state, action) {
  // your code
}

let s = []
s = cartReducer(s, { type: 'added', item: { id: 1, name: 'pen', price: 10 } })
s = cartReducer(s, { type: 'added', item: { id: 1, name: 'pen', price: 10 } })
s = cartReducer(s, { type: 'added', item: { id: 2, name: 'ink', price: 50 } })
console.log(JSON.stringify(s))
console.log(s.reduce((t, i) => t + i.price * i.qty, 0))
s = cartReducer(s, { type: 'qty_set', id: 1, qty: 0 })
console.log(JSON.stringify(s))
challenges.explain: Because the reducer is pure, it can be unit tested without rendering, and it returns new arrays and objects so React's Object.is comparison sees the change. Verified by running the solution in Node: the output matches.

challenges.title: Normalise an API response
challenges.prompt: Write toRecipe(meal) that turns a TheMealDB-style object (fields i1..i3 for ingredient names and m1..m3 for measures) into { id, ingredients: [{ name, measure }] }. Trim values and skip empty ingredient names.
challenges.explain: Normalising once keeps API shapes out of components. JSON.stringify omits the undefined measure for salt. Verified by running the solution in Node: output matches.
